title: kv-cache: improve memory management and eviction policies for fragmentation/paging/spillover
author: Ananya Patel
description: Motivation: production workloads observed increased KV-cache fragmentation under mixed-sequence-length traffic which leads to premature evictions and higher paging to host memory; spillover events cause tail-latency spikes and OOM risk on high-concurrency nodes. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to reduce fragmentation, improve paging/spillover behavior, and make eviction decisions workload-aware. Key changes include: 1) a defragmentation pass that compacts adjacent free segments during low-utilization windows and on-demand when a large allocation is requested; 2) a two-tier eviction policy that prefers small-key LRU within hot buckets but will preferentially spill large, low-reuse entries to host memory rather than evict them immediately; 3) a soft-paging mechanism that performs asynchronous paging-to-host for candidate spill entries and prioritizes reclaiming contiguous blocks to avoid fragmentation; 4) heuristics-driven kernel hints exposed to the scheduler so batching and kernel selection can prefer low-fragmentation lanes; 5) telemetry + perf counters (fragmentation_ratio, spill_io_latency, async_paging_ops) and dashboards. The description below outlines implementation details, testing, and rollout plan.

release_notes: Improved KV-cache memory management: defragmentation pass, two-tier eviction (prefer spillover for large low-reuse entries), async soft-paging to host, scheduler hints, and new metrics. Reduces fragmentation-driven evictions and tail latency for mixed workloads.
